acceptance: A unit test feeds a 403 rate-limit response followed by success and shows `pr-arm` waits and then evaluates the gate, without arming in between.
With the budget exhausted, the outcome line reads as waiting on the rate limit and names the reset time; exit status distinguishes it from a real refusal.
A secondary-rate-limit response (`Retry-After`) is handled the same way.
context: 2026-11-13, merged from a dropped duplicate (pr-arm-wait-stops-on-transient-github-errors-20261112): the same exit was seen twice more on 2026-11-12 while arming PR #4170 with WAIT=60 and WAIT=90, with 56 and 77 minutes left: `pr-arm: refusing: stopped waiting, the trunk check refuses: the trunk state could not be read: gh run list failed: HTTP 403: API rate limit exceeded`. A third wait on that pull request ended on a server error, not a rate limit: `review-gate: error: cannot read #4170 after 3 attempts: GitHub returned HTTP 503`; a 5xx on any read inside the wait should be treated the same way. The message comes from `scripts/pr_arm.py`. Guardrail to keep: an unreadable trunk or review-gate state must never arm; the change is to keep waiting inside the WAIT budget, and to refuse as today without WAIT or when it runs out. Worth measuring while here: how many REST calls one 3-minute wait cycle makes, since the loop itself spends the shared quota.
description:
Gap seen three times on 2026-11-12 (PR #4169 twice, PR #4175 once). While waiting, `pr-arm` calls `gh run list` for the trunk check; when the account's REST quota is exhausted (several agent sessions share one user) it prints `trunk-arm-gate: refusing: gh run list failed: HTTP 403: API rate limit exceeded` and exits non-zero with most of the `WAIT` budget unused. The reset time is known (`gh api rate_limit` does not count against the quota) and was 3 minutes away in the first case. Each caller then has to notice, compute the reset and start again, which is the hand-written loop the guide forbids.

Expected: within the `WAIT` budget, a 403 rate-limit response is treated as waiting, not refusal: sleep until the reported reset (bounded by the remaining budget), then continue. Outside the budget, exit with an outcome that names the reset time.

Guardrails: never treat an unreadable trunk state as passing; arming still requires a successful read. No retry on other 4xx responses. `scripts/pr_arm.py` and `scripts/trunk_revert.py` currently contain no rate-limit handling.
